english: Consider the $n$ observations $3,7,11,\ldots,4n-1$, which are in arithmetic progression. When one more observation, equal to the arithmetic mean of these $n$ observations, is included, the variance of the $n+1$ observations is $120$. Then the largest of the original $n$ observations is
hindi: समान्तर श्रेढ़ी में स्थित $n$ प्रेक्षणों $3,7,11,\ldots,4n-1$ पर विचार कीजिए। जब इन $n$ प्रेक्षणों के समान्तर माध्य के बराबर एक और प्रेक्षण सम्मिलित किया जाता है, तब $n+1$ प्रेक्षणों का प्रसरण $120$ है। तब मूल $n$ प्रेक्षणों में सबसे बड़ा प्रेक्षण है
solution: Variance of an AP with common difference $d$: $\dfrac{d^2(n^2-1)}{12}=\dfrac{4(n^2-1)}{3}$
Adding the mean keeps $\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2$ and the mean, so the new variance $=\dfrac{n}{n+1}\cdot\dfrac{4(n^2-1)}{3}=\dfrac{4n(n-1)}{3}$
solution_full: For $n$ terms of an AP with common difference $d$, the variance is $\dfrac{d^2(n^2-1)}{12}$; here $d=4$, so $\sigma^2=\dfrac{4(n^2-1)}{3}$.
The extra observation equals $\bar x$, so the mean of the $n+1$ observations is still $\bar x$, and the extra deviation is $0$.
Check: the AP $3,7,\ldots,39$ has mean $21$ and variance $132$; with $21$ added the variance is $\dfrac{10\cdot132}{11}=120$.
originality_note: New: an AP data set is enlarged by its own mean, which scales the variance by n/(n+1), so the AP variance formula leads to a quadratic in n (way 5: AP variance formula and the definition of variance of ungrouped data). Closest known: 'variance of an AP with n terms'. Different because: the variance given is that of the enlarged set; the plain formula gives n^2 = 91, which has no integer root.
